headline: Two short faster runs now sit where the huge Åre trail block used to be. The restart holds its top-end range, but weekly cadence and a fresh threshold reading are both still missing. Strength stays the quiet corner.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The shape of the last two weeks is a hard pivot: the enormous Swedish trail block — long, slow, Z1-dominated time on feet — has given way to two short, sharp road runs that reach into the upper zones. That's a deliberate change of character, not a decline, and the deep base underneath it hasn't gone anywhere. What's genuinely lagging is loading rhythm on both fronts: only three lifts in four weeks, none clustered, and running frequency since the restart still unproven beyond a pair. Steps stay high even on rest days, so background movement is carrying real daily load the tracked sessions don't show. The recovery and cardio-load streams read as quiet-to-detraining, which fits the low tracked-session count more than it reflects the actual body of work banked this month.
sections.trends: The medium-term picture is genuinely lopsided: the recent four-week block dwarfs the prior one, driven almost entirely by those big trail days, and year-to-date distance is nearly four times where it sat this time last year. That's a real, durable expansion of base — the kind of year that builds ultra capacity. The current cyclical dip in tracked load after the trail block is exactly the sort of consolidation that fits year-round hybrid readiness, so long as the running cadence re-establishes rather than trailing off. The shape makes sense; the open question is whether the next fortnight confirms rhythm or drifts.
sections.threshold: The threshold reading is now the oldest signal on the board by a wide margin, and nothing since has come close to refreshing it — the trail block was almost entirely aerobic-floor work, and the two runs back, while they touch the top end, are too short and too intermittent to serve as a sustained threshold probe. So the honest position is uncertainty: aerobic base is demonstrably deep, but where the actual threshold and VO2max sit right now is a genuine blind spot rather than a known quantity. A controlled sustained tempo would resolve that faster than more short mixed efforts.
sections.zones: The two restart runs are the opposite of the trail block in distribution — where the Åre days were pure Z1 floor, these move through Z2, Z3 and briefly into Z4, but the shape reads as varied-terrain drift-up rather than a targeted session, with a lot of time in the Z3 grey band and no sustained anchor in any one zone. For rebuilding top-end feel after a long slow block that's fine as a bridge, but it isn't yet either a clean easy run or a clean quality session. Nothing here needs correcting — just worth noting the intent of each run is still a little diffuse.
sections.hr_comparison: The most recent lift captured no HR at all, so the strength-intensity blind spot flagged earlier hasn't closed. The lifts that do carry HR sit in a believable working range for functional work, mostly low-to-moderate with occasional pushes higher, consistent across the earlier sessions. Where both a run and an estimated line exist, the numbers track sensibly together — no source disagreement worth acting on.
sections.calendar: The calendar shows a clear regime change mid-month: a dense cluster of big trail days, then a gap, then two shorter road runs — bursty rather than metronomic. Strength appears as isolated singles with long spacing, never a repeating slot. The running side has enough history to trust it re-forms; the strength side is the one where the pattern itself, not just the volume, is the thing to watch.
sections.personal_bests: The short-distance PBs were set almost exactly a year ago in a sharper, speed-focused phase — current training has been base and durability, not speed, so those marks aren't in realistic near-term reach without a dedicated block. The ultra/50K mark, by contrast, sits much closer to this year's demonstrated capacity given the trail volume banked, and would be the more plausible target if a long effort were on the horizon.

watch_items: Watch whether running settles into a repeating weekly cadence now that the restart is two runs deep but still unconfirmed as a rhythm.
Watch for a single sustained tempo effort — the threshold reading has now aged past the point where the base can be assumed to still map to it.
Watch whether strength moves from isolated singles into any kind of recurring slot, and whether the next lift captures HR.
Watch whether the short runs sharpen into distinct easy-vs-quality intents rather than staying in the mixed grey-zone drift.
